description: The series for one market or a few (max 10): one row per market per interval over a trailing window, ordered by interval then market. Pick bar (1d, the default, for one row per day, or 1h for one row per completed hour). Answers 'is this move backed by real flow' and 'how has positioning built up'. ending_day defaults to the last complete interval. The whole answer is capped, so markets times window_days (times 24 at bar 1h) must stay inside the row cap; the response states the window it used.

bar.description:
`1d` (the default) for completed UTC days, `1h` for completed UTC hours.
An interval, at either grain, is stamped by the instant it **closes** —
an hourly `…T09:00:00Z` is the hour that ended at 09:00.

columns.description:
Fields to return per row, from `list_fields`. The interval column
(`day` at 1d, `hour` at 1h) and `coin` are always included.

ending_day.description:
The last interval to include: `YYYY-MM-DD` or `latest` at `bar: 1d`, a
completed `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:00:00Z` (the hour that *ended* there) or
`latest` at `bar: 1h`.

window_days.description:
Length of the trailing window in days, 1..365. Defaults to 7. At
`bar: 1h` one window day is 24 hourly rows.

name: query_series

as_of.description: The last interval in the series.

bar.description: The grain this answer was computed at: `1d` or `1h`.

eligible_count.description:
The markets you asked for, after the plan's slice and your filter were
intersected.

matched_count.description:
How many of the requested markets the series actually has rows for — less
than `eligible_count` when one of them has no data in the window.

visible_count.description: Markets in your plan's slice with a row on the last interval.

window_days.description: The window the trailing fields were computed over, in days.
